question.text: How many Fifth Circuit news announcements concerning the Judge Ada Brown misconduct proceeding will be dated November 1–12, 2026?
question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves by counting the entries displayed in the Fifth Circuit's News & Announcements listing filtered to November 2026 (https://www.ca5.uscourts.gov/news?month=11&year=2026) as of 5:00 p.m. Central Time (23:00 UTC) on November 13, 2026. Count each entry whose listing date is between November 1 and November 12, 2026 (inclusive) and which concerns the judicial misconduct proceeding involving U.S. District Judge Ada E. Brown — that is, the entry's title or linked document(s) name Judge Ada Brown, or reference Complaint No. 05-26-90177, Complaint No. 05-26-90196, or the Fifth Circuit Judicial Council's proceedings against her — and the entry counts even if the substance of the underlying document remains confidential or undisclosed. Entries unrelated to that matter (for example CM/ECF maintenance notices, vacancy announcements, proposed rule amendments, or oral-argument notices) are not counted, and where the same document appears in more than one entry it is counted once. Inclusion is determined by the date shown in the listing's date column, not by a date written into an entry's title. The resolved value is that count: for example, if the listing shows one qualifying entry dated November 3, 2026 and another dated November 12, 2026, the question resolves as 2; if it shows no qualifying entries, it resolves as 0.
question.fine_print: Entries whose listing date is November 13, 2026 or later are not counted, and an entry dated November 1–12, 2026 that is first displayed after the 5:00 p.m. Central Time snapshot on November 13, 2026 is not counted. If that listing or its month filter is unavailable, an archived copy of the listing or of the court's news pages (such as a Wayback Machine snapshot from November 13, 2026), or [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions) reporting the same postings, will be used to establish what was displayed.

research:

## 4. Base rates
- Since the court began posting about the matter, it has posted 3 Brown entries in 12 days (October 19-30). That is about one every 4 days, each tied to a discrete event: the leak, the written-questions order, and the missed interview.
- Before October 19 there were 0 Brown entries, including in September, when orders were issued but kept confidential.
- From October 31 to November 3 there were 0 entries, so the posting has paused since the interview.
- The whole site averages about 1.5 to 2 entries a month in 2025-2026, so any non-Brown posting is rare too.
- Each posting so far followed a public trigger. The next statutory step is the committee's report to the Council under § 353(c). Under § 360 that report is confidential, but a Council order could be made public under Rule 24.
- Comparison: the Pauline Newman matter took months from committee action to a published Council order.

## 5. Other forecasts
- I found no Polymarket, Kalshi, Manifold or Metaculus market on this question or the Brown proceeding.
- The market prices you collected (county judge races, a DOJ Watergate investigation, AI model releases) are unrelated.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- Any day: the committee files its report, the Council issues an order (censure, a disability certification, a request to retire, or a referral to the Judicial Conference), or the court extends or changes the interim reassignment. I found no announced dates.
- Brown could leak documents again, sue, or speak publicly. In October a leak prompted a same-cycle statement from the Council (posted on October 19, two days after it).
- 2026-11-11: Veterans Day, a federal holiday, so the court is unlikely to post that day.
- The interim reassignment runs until about December 29, three months from September 29. That is after this question's window.
- 2026-11-13, 5 p.m. CT: the listing is snapshotted for resolution.
